report.source_text: After completing the treatment, the patient fully recovered. End-of-treatment examinations revealed no abnormalities, and there were no adverse or unexpected events during the treatment and follow-up period. Her estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and renal function test results were within the reference range. Follow-up sonography revealed no abnormal findings, with standard kidney size, shape, and cortical echogenicity. There was no evidence of hydronephrosis, stones, or structural abnormalities. clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old girl presented with acute abdominal pain and a left upper abdominal mass. Initial workup included normal routine labs and imaging (ultrasonography and CT) which identified a large, heterogeneous, encapsulated mass in the left upper abdomen, distinct from the left kidney. The patient underwent laparotomy, and the mass was surgically resected. Macroscopic and microscopic pathology confirmed features consistent with Wilms tumor, with positive nuclear staining for WT1 and absence of residual kidney parenchyma, leading to the diagnosis of extrarenal Wilms tumor with favorable histology. Post-surgery, the patient received 19 weeks of chemotherapy (EE4A regimen). She fully recovered, with no adverse events or recurrence observed during follow-up.
